process_notes.Federal Register notices (BLM, FS, DOE,: NOIs, notices of availability of EAs/EISs, RODs and presidential-permit notices; list via the federalregister.gov API (search plus agency filters) and EPA's weekly EIS filing notices (read on govinfo.gov). Only about 20 project-specific transmission notices in 2023-2026, mostly big western lines Line Watch already has (SunZia, Greenlink West/North, Cross-Tie, GridLiance West, Silver Rock, Grain Belt, Crossroads-Hobbs-Roadrunner, CHPE, Basin Electric border lines). It turned up 2 new projects (NPPD R-Project and GTC Dresden-Talbot 500 kV) and 2 that fall outside the window (North Plains Connector, in service end of 2032; Ironwood, Dec 2031). Most EAs and FONSIs never appear in the Federal Register, so on its own this source has low yield.
process_notes.Federal Permitting Dashboard (permits.pe: FAST-41 covered and transparency projects. The HTML site returns 403 to scripts, but the official Socrata data portal (data.permits.performance.gov, dataset mcm3-xbid) is open and has every project with milestones. It lists only 16 transmission projects. All are listed in Line Watch or out of scope except Ironwood 500 kV (Horizon West, CAISO), which became FAST-41 in Oct 2026 but has a Dec 2031 in-service date, so I excluded it. There are no transmission transparency projects. Useful for milestone dates (Silver Rock ROD target 2028-07; Royal Slope final decision 2027-03), poor for finding new projects.
process_notes.BLM National NEPA Register / ePlanning: Every BLM NEPA record (CX, DNA, EA, EIS) with right-of-way details. The search page calls a public JSON endpoint (eplanning.blm.gov/searchresults/), so I could pull it by keyword. This was the most useful source. Most hits are oil-field distribution lines, renewals and herbicide work, but it surfaced short western lines and gen-ties that grid-operator lists miss: Reid Gardner-Tortoise #2 230 kV, Pecos-Quasar 138 kV, Boulder Valley 230 kV gen-tie, Boulder Flats 230 kV, TWE HAE 500 kV switchyard, Sierra Solar/Lantern 345 kV and Schnebly Coulee 230 kV. Many other hits were already listed (Arida 2a-Mohave, Eagle Eye-Harcuvar, Harquahala North, Nighthawk fold, Lucky Star, Rock Creek, Eureka, Delamar 500 kV). Gen-ties analysed inside solar-project EISs are not covered by a name search.
process_notes.Forest Service Schedules of Proposed Act: The Forest Service stopped issuing SOPA reports in 2025. Projects now sit on per-forest 'Projects' pages, there is no national list, and www.fs.usda.gov/sopa returns 403. Web searches of fs.usda.gov project pages found only 69-138 kV rebuilds (AEP South Bluefield-Wythe, Elihu-Wofford, LPEA Bayfield-Pagosa 115 kV), renewals (Dominion Line 550), already-listed lines (Mount Storm-Valley 500 kV, Greenlink North, Cross-Tie) and a cancelled 500 kV special use permit (Draconis, Prescott NF). Low yield.
process_notes.USDA Rural Utilities Service environment: RUS EAs/FONSIs and EISs/RODs for co-op projects it may finance; the fullest list is the RD 'Rural Utilities Service' environmental-studies page (by borrower), plus the older 'Assessments' and 'Impact Statements' lists; Federal Register carries almost none of these (only 2 RUS electric EIS notices 2023-2026). Moderately useful: ~20 transmission-related entries, many old (2010-2016) or 69 kV; yielded Dresden-Talbot County 500 kV (ROD Feb 2026), Dry Creek-Smyrna 161 kV, SGS-JEA 230 kV structure replacement, and small 138-161 kV interconnection lines inside generation EAs (Ripley, Turney, Hickory Grove, Liberty RICE); confirmed stage for several GTC projects. Most co-op work runs under categorical exclusions that are not posted.
process_notes.WAPA (all regions, NEPA pages, ten-year: WAPA regional NEPA pages (EIS/EA/CX lists by year), DSW ten-year capital plan books, HQ Environmental Review page, TIP project list. Useful for rebuilds of WAPA's own 161-230 kV lines (Bouse-Kofa, Gila-Knob, Parker-Blythe #2) and interconnection switchyards (MPP-Q01, Beale); most UGP/RM items are 115 kV or already listed via SPP; CXs are mostly maintenance. Rocky Mountain region page did not render (link-wrapped) and RM has no current major line project beyond completed rebuilds.
process_notes.BPA (GERP, transmission plan, capital re: BPA 2025 Attachment K transmission plan, GERP 1.0/2.0 summaries and Aug 2026 schedule table, and quarterly major-capital status reports. Useful: most GERP 1.0 items were already listed; added Bonanza hub substation, Ross-Rivergate, Big Eddy-Quenett Creek, Keeler-Horizon #2 and a Ponderosa solar 230 kV tie. GERP 2.0 lines (Lower Columbia-Bonanza-NOB 500 kV, Schultz-Olympia, Coulee-Columbia-Schultz, North of Pearl, Salem area) and Big Eddy-Chemawa, La Pine-Bonanza and Schultz-Raver are dated 2032-2035, outside the window. BPA cluster-study network upgrades were not itemized publicly enough to add.

Very useful: names every new POI switching station (often unnamed 'tap' ring buses) and shared network-upgrade line rebuilds years before STEP/NTC; ~10% of 230 kV+/138 kV+ items matched the listed file (by UID or ends). Cross-checked each against GIActive status (withdrawn sponsors dropped) and COD. In-service dates mostly left blank because the studies give lead times, not dates; queue CODs quoted in stage_basis.

Note RTOE (Tri-State/WAPA RMR/PRPA) requests now appear here but their studies are on Tri-State's OASIS, not SPP's GI pages, so most Tri-State POI stations (Burlington-Wray, LRS-Wayne Child, Big Bear, Duck Creek, Many Trails, Towner) could not be documented and were not reported.

Some tables are images.

Phase 1/2 upgrades change a lot and most firm GI upgrades already appear in the listed MTEP25 Appendix A rows, so yield was low; Hazel Creek - Scott County 345 kV and 2nd Callaway - Bland 345 kV appear only as study-phase upgrades with no current status and were not reported.

Most ERAS POIs with '(new)' substations (Smalling, West Fork Creek, Green Acres, RiverPlex, Odyssey) were already listed; new finds came from Entergy Louisiana's LPSC Westlake/Waterford 6 testimony.

Very useful for new 345 kV switching stations: 508 not-yet-energized tap POIs; most IA-signed ones already appear in TPIT/Line Watch under station names (Gulch, Montura, Claror, Paladio...), leaving ~40 distinct new POI stations (IA-signed = planned, FIS-complete-only = proposed). GINR never names the TSP and rarely the station; FIS-started-only requests (~300) were not added.
process_notes.ERCOT TPIT cross-check: Used only to dedupe GINR, but it showed ~30 Oct-2026 TPIT 345/765 kV rows missing from Line Watch (Raider, Settlers, Faraday loop, Solstice/Duende 765 kV, Surreal, Hays Hill, Benedum, Jacaranda-Paulownia, several Oncor/CPS rebuilds); added them.
